title: Interpreter use and patient-reported understanding: an umbrella review to inform a network interpreter standard
subtitle: Overview of reviews on professional, ad hoc, video and in-person interpretation and patient-reported understanding
statement: In a four-hospital network, fewer than half of eligible inpatient encounters with patients who prefer a language other than English used a professional interpreter, and the equity committee must set a standard for professional interpretation and choose between investing in in-person or video interpreters. Many reviews exist but disagree, and patient-reported understanding is the outcome the committee cares about most. An umbrella review would show where the reviews agree, how good they are and where evidence is missing.
whoAffected: Patients who prefer a language other than English and their families, clinicians, interpreters and the network's language services and equity committee.
whatHurts: Without professional interpretation, patients may not understand diagnoses, consent or discharge instructions, and errors by ad hoc interpreters go unnoticed.
currentPractice: Professional interpreters in person or by video on request; frequent use of family members, bilingual colleagues or clinicians' own limited language skills.
whyNow: An equity committee decision in April 2027 on an interpreter standard and investment, and a widely repeated claim about video that nobody can trace.
constraints: No research funding; one language services analyst for two days a week from October 2026 to March 2027; findings due to the equity committee in April 2027; no patient-level data will be collected for this review.
patientCenteredGoal: Every patient who prefers another language understands their diagnosis, consent and discharge plan.
summary: Problem framed as an umbrella review to inform an interpreter standard and investment choice.
